Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Muna Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Muna Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muna. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Muna Regency. 5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their roles normally again both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfill the needs of victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in the context of implementing activities for the prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is temporary housing provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life. 30.

Article 14
(1) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 10 letter d, include:
a. shelter services or safe houses;
b. assistance services by social workers;
c. peer group services; and
d. victim family strengthening services.
(2) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by specially trained officers.
(3) Social rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of social affairs.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 20
(1) Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be carried out through an integrated service mechanism.
(2) The integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be established at the regency level, sub-district level and village or urban village level.

Article 11
(1) Complaint services as referred to in Article 10 letter a, include:
a. services for providing information regarding rights and services provided to victims;
b. toll-free complaint telephone services;
c. outreach services; and
d. consultation services.
(2) Complaint services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization that handles affairs of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 30
(1) Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Universities that carry out protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER VIII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 24
(1) The community and business sector have the right to participate in the prevention of cases of violence against women and children, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out individually or collectively, either personally or institutionally.

BAB II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Protection of women and children victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. gender equality and justice; c. non-discrimination; d. protection of victims' rights; e. legal certainty.

3.8.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 4 explicitly lists victims’ rights including “f. pelayanan bimbingan rohani” (spiritual guidance services). Also, Pasal 1 angka 20 defines “Pendampingan” as including “bimbingan rohani” (spiritual guidance). Therefore the policy does provide for religious/spiritual counselling/support. The retrieved English candidates accurately reflect this (e.g., Article 4(f) “spiritual guidance services”). The judge’s “Yes” is consistent with the source text, so the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

5.6.translated_snippet: (8) Implementation of prevention of violence against women and children shall be carried out by involving community organizations, non-governmental organizations, legal aid institutions, business sector, communities, children and adolescent groups, mass media and other related parties.
5.6.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly lists mass media among the parties to be involved in implementing prevention of violence against women and children, recognizing media as a stakeholder.

CHAPTER IX MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 25
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations that implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

Article 26
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

5.6.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 9 ayat (8) states that prevention implementation is carried out by involving various parties including “media massa” (mass media): “Pelaksanaan pencegahan ... dilakukan dengan melibatkan ... media massa dan pihak lainnya yang terkait.” This is direct media engagement/recognition of media as a stakeholder in prevention activities. The retrieved English passage [5.6-16] correctly includes “mass media,” and the judge’s rationale matches the Indonesian provision. Therefore the golden label “No” appears wrong; it should be “Yes” given the explicit mention of media involvement.
